newsitem.title: USA: Conoco, Reading & Bates order second drillship.
newsitem.headline: Conoco, Reading & Bates order second drillship.

text.p: Conoco and Reading & Bates Corp have ordered a second $200 million drill ship for exploration in the Gulf of Mexico and in international deep waters, the companies said on Thursday.

The ship, capable of drilling in up to 10,000 feet (3,048 metres) of water, will be acquired by a joint venture owned 60 percent by Reading & Bates and 40 percent by Conoco, a DuPont unit, the companies said.
The 721-foot (219.8 metre) long ships will be built by Samsung Heavy Industries of South Korea, with the first set for delivery in 1998 and the second in early 1999.

"A second state-of-the-art drill ship will allow us to efficiently carry out our deep water exploration program during a period of time when we envision a serious shortage of available deep water rigs," Conoco President Archie Dunham said.

Conoco holds drilling rights on 15 million acres of deep water tracts worldwide, including 130 tracts in the Gulf of Mexico and leases in the Caribbean, offshore Norway, the United Kingdom and New Zealand, the company said.
In October 1996, the companies formed a venture to build a drill ship for Conoco's $400 million, five-year Gulf of Mexico drilling program by Reading & Bates.
